1.title: From the Beginning
1.context: The letter opens with no greeting and no signature. Its first sentence piles up the senses: heard, seen with our own eyes, gazed upon, touched with our own hands, naming the thing handled the Word of life.
1.question: What does it change for you that the faith rests on witnesses who could touch what they proclaimed?

1.title: The Life Revealed
1.context: The eternal life was with the Father and was revealed; the witnesses' verbs are seen, testified, and proclaim. The telling stresses the order: with the Father, revealed to them, proclaimed to the readers.
1.question: Where have you received the message second-hand and found it trustworthy?

1.title: Fellowship with the Father and with His Son
1.context: The proclamation's goal is fellowship, a shared life the readers are invited inside, and the fellowship's address is given: with the Father and with his Son, Jesus Christ, named for the first time in the letter here.
1.question: What does fellowship with God look like in your ordinary week?

1.title: So That Our Joy May Be Complete
1.context: The writer never names himself in this letter. Tradition has long ascribed it to John the apostle, and the telling names that as tradition; the book stands in the undated group of this series. His own stated purpose closes the opening: we write these things so that our joy may be complete.
1.question: Whose joy is bound up with your believing, besides your own?

2.title: The Message We Have Heard
2.context: The message is delivered with its chain of custody: heard from him, announced to you. Its claim is total: God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all.
2.question: What would change if you let this one claim measure the rest of your beliefs about God?

2.title: Walking in the Light
2.context: The claim of fellowship is tested by the walk. Walking in the light brings two gifts at once: fellowship with one another, and cleansing from all sin by the blood of Jesus.
2.question: What is one step of walking in the light that is yours to take this week?

2.title: If We Say We Have No Sin
2.context: The first liar in the letter is the man describing himself. Claiming no sin is called self-deception, and the warning is written in we-language, inside the fellowship's own circle.
2.question: Where are you most tempted to describe yourself more generously than the light allows?

2.title: Faithful and Just to Forgive
2.context: Confession carries a double promise grounded in God's character: he is faithful, so the forgiveness is sure; he is just, so it is right. The outcome runs past pardon to cleansing from all unrighteousness.
2.question: Is there a sin you have named to everyone except God, or to God in every way except plainly?

2.title: His Word Is Not in Us
2.context: The sharpest form of the claim: to say we have not sinned makes God out to be a liar, since he has said otherwise. The chapter ends here with no softening sentence after it.
2.question: Why do you think denial of sin is treated as an accusation against God, not only a mistake about oneself?

3.title: We Have an Advocate
3.context: My little children is the letter's fatherly address, used here for the first time. The aim is that they not sin; the provision, if anyone does, is an advocate before the Father, Jesus Christ the Righteous One, himself the atoning sacrifice for the sins of the whole world.
3.question: Do you go to God after sinning as if you had an advocate, or as if you had only a judge?

3.title: If We Keep His Commandments
3.context: Knowledge of God is tested by obedience. The claim I know him stands in its own quotation and is judged a lie when the commandments are not kept.
3.question: What would your life say you know about God, if your words were removed?

3.title: The Love of God Perfected
3.context: Keeping his word is where the love of God reaches its goal in a person. The contrast with the liar is not more information but a kept word.
3.question: Which of God's words are you currently keeping, and which are you merely admiring?

3.title: Walk as Jesus Walked
3.context: Abiding in him is measured by a walk against a walk: as Jesus walked. The standard is not admiration or confession but step-shaped likeness.
3.question: What is one concrete step of Jesus' walk that you could imitate this week?

4.title: An Old Commandment, and New
4.context: The commandment is old, had from the beginning of the readers' hearing, and new, because the darkness is fading and the true light is already shining. Both claims stand at once.
4.question: Which old truth has become new to you lately because of the light you now live in?

4.title: Still in the Darkness
4.context: Hatred of a brother locates a man whatever his claims: he is still in the darkness. Love remains in the light, and the hater's darkness ends in blindness about his own direction.
4.question: Is there a relationship where your claim to light and your actual walk disagree?

4.title: Children, Fathers, Young Men
4.context: The letter pauses to address its readers in a pattern: children forgiven through his name, fathers who know him who is from the beginning, young men who have overcome the evil one. Whether the names mark ages or stages, the text does not say.
4.question: Which line of the address sounds most like your own life right now?

4.title: Strong, and the Word Abides in You
4.context: The second round fills the young men out: strong, the word of God abiding in them, the evil one overcome. The warnings of this letter are written to the established, not to outsiders.
4.question: What has God already established in you that you tend to underrate?

5.title: Do Not Love the World
5.context: World here is the world's system of wanting, not the earth God made. Two loves are treated as tenants who cannot share one house: if anyone loves the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
5.question: Which love is resident in you, by the evidence of your wanting?

5.title: The Desires of the Flesh, the Eyes, the Pride of Life
5.context: The world's whole inventory is three lines: the desires of the flesh, the desires of the eyes, and the pride of life, and none of it is from the Father. The verse itself breaks around its list, and the telling carries it that way.
5.question: Which of the three does most of your wanting run through?

5.title: The World Is Passing Away
5.context: The reason for the refusal is not the world's strength but its departure: it is passing away with its desires, while whoever does the will of God remains forever. The closing paragraph gathers the letter's method: every claim checked against a reality.
5.question: What are you loving that is already in the act of leaving?

6.title: It Is the Last Hour
6.context: An antichrist was expected; many antichrists have appeared instead, and their arrival is named as the evidence of the hour. No timetable is built on the claim.
6.question: How does naming the hour you live in change how seriously you take it?

6.title: They Went Out from Us
6.context: The departed came from inside the fellowship, and their leaving is read as revelation: they went out because they did not belong. No group is identified beyond the writer's words.
6.question: How do you hold grief and clarity together when someone walks away from the faith?

6.title: An Anointing from the Holy One
6.context: Against the departed stands the gift that remains: an anointing from the Holy One, and readers who know the truth. The letter arms people who already hold the truth; it does not treat them as empty.
6.question: What truth do you already hold that you need to act on rather than relearn?

6.title: Who Is the Liar
6.context: The liar in full is defined: the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ. Denying the Son and having the Father are treated as impossible together, in either direction.
6.question: Why does this letter refuse every route to the Father that runs around the Son?

6.title: Let What You Heard Remain in You
6.context: The assignment is remaining: what was heard from the beginning, the promise of eternal life, and the anointing that teaches. Deception fails against people who stay.
6.question: What did you hear at the beginning that you most need to let remain?

7.title: Confident and Unashamed at His Coming
7.context: Remaining in Christ is aimed at his appearing: confidence and no shame before him at his coming. Righteousness practiced is traced to birth: everyone who practices it has been born of him.
7.question: What would you do differently today if you expected to stand before him unashamed?

7.title: Called Children of God
7.context: Behold invites a long look at the love measured by the name it gives: children of God, and that is what we are. The world's non-recognition is explained in a line: it did not know him.
7.question: Do you treat your name, child of God, as a title or as the fact of what you are?

7.title: We Will Be Like Him
7.context: Now children of God; what we will be not yet revealed, except for likeness: when he appears we will be like him, for we will see him as he is. The hope purifies the one who holds it.
7.question: What is this hope currently purifying in your habits?

7.title: He Appeared to Take Away Sins
7.context: Sin is defined as lawlessness, and the practicing passages are carried at full strength as written: no one who remains in him keeps on sinning. The Son was revealed to destroy the works of the devil, who has been sinning from the very start.
7.question: How do you hold the letter's strong words about sin together with its promise of an advocate?

7.title: Born of God
7.context: The strongest sentence rests on the birth: God's seed abides in him; he cannot go on sinning, because he has been born of God. The distinction is then stated between the children of God and the children of the devil, by righteousness practiced and a brother loved.
7.question: What in your life is best explained by a birth rather than by your effort?

8.title: The Message from the Beginning
8.context: Love one another is stated as the message itself, heard from the beginning and carried through every test in the letter.
8.question: Is loving your brothers the center of your faith, or a department of it?

8.title: Do Not Be Like Cain
8.context: Cain is carried in the letter's compression: he belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother, because his own deeds were evil while his brother's were righteous. His whole story is told in the Genesis book of this series. The world's hatred is then named as no surprise.
8.question: Have you felt the friction of righteous deeds in a place that preferred evil ones?

8.title: Passed from Death to Life
8.context: The passage from death to life is said to be known by one evidence: we love our brothers. Hatred is weighed in the letter's hardest words, as membership in Cain's category.
8.question: What does your love for the brothers tell you about your own standing?

8.title: He Laid Down His Life for Us
8.context: Love is defined by an event: Jesus laid down his life for us. The definition becomes a debt immediately: we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.
8.question: What would laying down your life for a brother look like at ordinary scale?

8.title: Not in Word, but in Action and Truth
8.context: The debt is brought to wallet scale: possessions in hand, a brother in need, compassion withheld, and the question answers itself. The charge closes: love in action and truth, not word and speech.
8.question: Where is your love currently all word, and what action is waiting?

9.title: We Will Assure Our Hearts
9.context: Love in action assures the heart in God's presence: by this we know we belong to the truth. Assurance here is a fruit of love, not only of argument.
9.question: What most often makes your heart shrink from God's presence?

9.title: God Is Greater Than Our Hearts
9.context: A condemning heart is appealed to a higher court: God is greater than our hearts, and he knows all things. The same total knowledge comforts the over-condemned and sobers the over-acquitted.
9.question: Which edge of this verse do you need more: the comfort or the sobering?

9.title: Confidence, and Whatever We Ask
9.context: An uncondemning heart has confidence before God, and the confidence has an address in prayer, inside a life of kept commandments rather than traded for them.
9.question: How does the state of your heart affect the boldness of your prayers?

9.title: His Commandment, Singular
9.context: The commandments gather into one with two halves: believe in the name of his Son, Jesus Christ, and love one another. Believing and loving are fused as a single instruction.
9.question: Which half of the one commandment comes easier to you, and which half exposes you?

9.title: By the Spirit He Has Given Us
9.context: The mutual remaining, God in us and we in him, is known by the Spirit he has given. The naming of the Spirit bridges into the warning that not every spirit is his.
9.question: How have you known God's presence from the inside of your own life?

10.title: Do Not Believe Every Spirit
10.context: Beloved opens a warning: belief is not to be indiscriminate, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. The spirits behind the teachers are to be tested.
10.question: Where have you been believing a voice you never tested?

10.title: Come in the Flesh
10.context: The test is one confession: Jesus Christ has come in the flesh. Its refusal is named the spirit of the antichrist, coming and already in the world, carried at the strength stated with no figure in any age matched to it.
10.question: Why is the flesh, real humanity, the battleground of this confession?

10.title: Greater Is He Who Is in You
10.context: The verdict is past tense: you have overcome them. The reason is a comparison of residents, he who is in you against he who is in the world, and the greater is named without argument.
10.question: Do you face deception as outnumbered, or as carrying the stronger indwelling?

10.title: The World Listens to Them
10.context: Speech from the world finds hearing in the world. Popularity is a matching of sources, not a test of truth.
10.question: Where has applause, yours or others', been standing in for a test you should have run?

10.title: The Spirit of Truth and the Spirit of Deception
10.context: The apostolic we returns as a test: whoever knows God listens to us. Hearing or refusing the testimony sorts the hearers, and the two spirits are named, truth and deception.
10.question: What testimony have you been refusing that your refusal itself might be evidence about?

11.title: Love Comes from God
11.context: The call to love one another is grounded in God's nature: love comes from God, and everyone who loves has been born of God and knows God.
11.question: Do you try to manufacture love, or receive it from its source?

11.title: God Is Love
11.context: The letter's second great claim matches its first: God is light, and God is love. Whoever does not love does not know God, whatever else he knows.
11.question: What does it do to your picture of God that love is what he is, not only what he does?

11.title: He Sent His One and Only Son
11.context: Love was revealed by a sending: God sent his one and only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. The nature of God is read off an act of God.
11.question: Where is your life currently running through him, and where around him?

11.title: Not That We Loved God
11.context: Love's definition runs backwards from instinct: not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins. Every later human love is a response, never the original.
11.question: What changes when you stop trying to be the origin of the love in your life?

11.title: No One Has Ever Seen God
11.context: The owing is drawn, and the paradox answered: no one has ever seen God, but if we love one another, God remains in us and his love is perfected in us. The invisible God becomes present in visible love.
11.question: Who experiences God's presence mainly through your love for the brothers?

12.title: The Savior of the World
12.context: The Spirit given, the testimony renewed with the opening's own verbs, seen and testify, and Jesus given the letter's largest title: the Savior of the world. Confession of him as God's Son carries the promise of mutual abiding.
12.question: What confession about Jesus is yours to make plainly?

12.title: Confidence on the Day of Judgment
12.context: God is love is repeated and aimed at a day: love perfected among us gives confidence on the day of judgment, stated with no timetable, grounded in likeness: in this world we are just like him.
12.question: Does the thought of that day find you confident, and on what ground?

12.title: Perfect Love Drives Out Fear
12.context: Fear is evicted, not managed: perfect love drives it out, because fear involves punishment. The fearful are described as not yet perfected in love, a stage to grow out of. The root predates everything: he first loved us.
12.question: What fear in you is still running on an expectation of punishment?

12.title: Whom He Has Seen, Whom He Has Not Seen
12.context: The liar charge returns on a plain matter of sight: love claimed for the unseen God while the seen brother is hated is graded a lie, with no third category offered.
12.question: Which is easier for you to claim love toward, and which does your life actually show?

12.title: Whoever Loves God Must Love His Brother
12.context: The love teaching closes in law, not summary: we have this commandment from him. The two loves four chapters have joined are joined in command at the end.
12.question: Is your love of God and your love of your brother growing together, or has one been asked to substitute for the other?

13.title: His Commandments Are Not Burdensome
13.context: The family circle closes: belief, birth, and love of the Father and his children in one sentence, and the commandments reframed as not burdensome.
13.question: Which commandment feels heaviest to you, and what would the letter say about that weight?

13.title: The Victory That Has Overcome the World
13.context: The world that must not be loved can be overcome, and the instrument is faith: everyone born of God overcomes, and the overcomer is the one who believes Jesus is the Son of God.
13.question: What part of the world most needs overcoming in your life, and is faith aimed at it?

13.title: By Water and Blood
13.context: The Son's coming is stated with its own correction, not by water alone but by water and blood, and the telling adds no theory beyond his insistence on both. The Spirit testifies, because the Spirit is the truth.
13.question: Where are you tempted to keep only half of what God insists on joining?

13.title: These Three Are in Agreement
13.context: Three witnesses are named, the Spirit, the water, and the blood, and their agreement is the stated fact; no other witnesses are added. God's testimony about his Son outranks human testimony, and refusing it makes God out to be a liar.
13.question: What testimony about Jesus have you been treating as smaller than people's opinions?

13.title: This Life Is in His Son
13.context: The testimony's content gathers the letter's promise: God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. The division is plain: whoever has the Son has life.
13.question: Is eternal life, for you, a location in a person or a possession you keep checking for?

14.title: So That You May Know
14.context: The letter's purpose is stated at the end: written to believers in the name of the Son of God, so that they may know they have eternal life. The tests were never meant to leave readers in suspense about their standing.
14.question: Do you know, in this letter's sense, or are you still guessing about the largest thing?

14.title: He Hears Us
14.context: Confidence before God has an address in prayer: asked according to his will, heard; and heard, in his case, means the asked thing already possessed.
14.question: What would you ask if you were sure of being heard?

14.title: A Sin Not Leading to Death
14.context: Prayer for a sinning brother is the instruction, an act of the letter's love. A sin that leads to death is named as a category, and no list is invented for either side; the distinction is carried exactly as drawn.
14.question: Who is the brother whose sin should have your prayers, and what would asking for his life look like?

14.title: We Know That the Son of God Has Come
14.context: The close runs on three we-knows: the born of God protected and untouchable by the evil one; we are of God while the world lies under the evil one's power; and the Son has come and given understanding, the letter's first knowledge come full circle.
14.question: Which of the three we-knows do you most need to live from this week?

14.title: Keep Yourselves from Idols
14.context: The letter ends without farewell or blessing, on the father's voice and a guard: little children, keep yourselves from idols. The telling leaves the line unexplained, where he leaves it. The undated group continues after this with the shortest letters in the New Testament.
14.question: What competes for the place in your life that the true God has claimed?
